title: Salesforce vs. Palantir Technologies: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
detail:
Salesforce vs. Palantir Technologies: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
Pamela Kock, The Motley Fool

CRM
PLTR
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Choosing between Salesforce (NYSE:CRM) and Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR) requires weighing mature, steady cash flow against high-octane growth. Both companies are now central players in the evolving landscape of enterprise software.

Salesforce focuses on managing customer relationships through a massive cloud ecosystem, while Palantir provides the underlying operating systems for data-driven decision-making. Investors often compare them because both are aggressively integrating artificial intelligence into their core offerings to capture a larger share of corporate IT budgets.

The case for Salesforce

Among tech stocks, Salesforce provides a comprehensive suite of cloud-based tools, including its Customer 360 platform and the newly launched Agentforce. The company serves a diverse global audience across sectors like financial services and healthcare, recently expanding its data capabilities through the acquisition of Informatica. No single customer accounts for more than 10% of revenue, providing a stable foundation for its subscription model.

In the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, revenue reached nearly $41.5 billion, representing a year-over-year increase of roughly 9.6%. This steady growth was accompanied by net income of approximately $7.5 billion, showing a net margin of close to 18%. These results show the company is transitioning from pure revenue expansion toward more robust bottom-line profitability.

As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.3x, showing the company uses a conservative amount of debt relative to its equity. The current ratio, which measures the ability to pay short-term obligations with short-term assets, is roughly 0.8x, and free cash flow reached nearly $14.4 billion in its latest fiscal year. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 23.4% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The case for Palantir Technologies

Palantir builds specialized platforms like Foundry and Gotham that allow organizations to integrate massive data sets for real-time analysis. Its Artificial Intelligence Platform (AIP) has become a primary growth driver, helping it reach over 1,000 total customers. However, the company faces customer concentration risk, as its top three clients accounted for approximately 16% of total revenue in its most recent annual report.

In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, revenue reached nearly $4.5 billion, a significant jump of roughly 56.2% compared with the prior fiscal year. The company reported net income of approximately $1.6 billion, resulting in a net margin of close to 36.3%. This surge in profitability highlights the scalability of its software platforms as more commercial enterprises adopt its AI tools.

title: Docusign embeds agreement platform directly into Salesforce
detail:
Docusign embeds agreement platform directly into Salesforce
Salesforce and Docusign deepen tie-up for contract automation. · Verdict · jackpress/Shutterstock.com.
Anwesha Pattanaik

Trading disclosure

US-based technology company Docusign has announced the expansion of its longstanding collaboration with Salesforce, introducing its Intelligent Agreement Management (IAM) platform directly within Salesforce, Slack, and Agentforce.

The integration allows revenue teams to manage and progress agreement workflows without switching between different tools.

The move aims to address challenges faced by sales teams that traditionally needed to navigate unstructured documents and separate file repositories to access agreement data.

By embedding Docusign's IAM platform natively into Salesforce applications, both companies seek to streamline deal processes and reduce delays, while providing real-time contract insights and highlighting hidden risks associated with document obligations.

Salesforce president and chief commercial officer Bill Patterson said: "Every agreement has the power to move a business forward, yet disconnected processes often stall growth.

"Building on two decades of partnership with Docusign, we're bringing agreement intelligence and workflows natively into Salesforce, Agentforce, and Slack so people and AI agents can turn executing agreements into a competitive advantage."

The enhanced integration also extends to Slackforce and the Headless Toolkit, facilitating access to Docusign's agreement management features across emerging agentic environments.

Docusign president and chief revenue officer Paula Hansen said: "By extending Docusign's integration across Salesforce, Agentforce, and Slack, we're putting agreement data directly into the hands of the teams closing and managing deals, rather than leaving it siloed in a separate platform.

"The same intelligence that closes a deal can flag the renewal, surface the expansion, and uncover the cross-sell. Agreements aren't a step in the process, they're a constant source of intelligence that drives a business forward."

According to the companies, sales teams using the integrated Docusign features can ask contract-related questions, generate agreements, and manage the full agreement lifecycle from drafting to final signature within their existing Salesforce CRM.

The system also offers AI-supported tools for contract review and renewal tracking, and enables teams to act on agreements within Slack conversations.

Docusign's latest updates focus on supporting deep, agentic workflows inside Salesforce Agentforce, allowing AI-driven contract management and workflow automation without leaving the CRM platform.

Last month, Salesforce launched Koa, a customer relationship management reasoning model developed for the Agentforce platform in collaboration with Nvidia.

"Docusign embeds agreement platform directly into Salesforce" was originally created and published by Verdict, a GlobalData owned brand.

Salesforce (CRM) stock has lost 3.8% over the past twelve months, trailing the 17.3% return of the S&P 500. Executives say their job with artificial intelligence is to deliver new value to customers. During the fiscal Q2 2027 earnings call on August 26, 2026, management described an upgrade that most of its users have not made yet.

Salesforce Wants Its Customers On Premium Editions

Salesforce is waiting to sell its customers an upgrade. The company packages its newest AI features within premium editions of its software, and management noted that clients seeking these features must move to higher-end tiers. One such feature combines an AI model with the data a customer already stores inside Salesforce.

Few users have made the transition so far. Only 5% of the people who use Salesforce's sales and service software have upgraded to the higher-end editions, according to management. Yet the company stated that customers that have started using Salesforce's AI agents already spend about twice as much a year with the company, on average.

Agentforce's Recurring Revenue Is Small Beside The Whole Company

Agentforce, the company's product for AI agents, reached $1.5 billion of annual recurring revenue in fiscal Q2 2027. That figure remains a small fraction of the $43.9 billion of revenue Salesforce generated over the last twelve months.

The growth opportunity lies in the software those upgrades are sold into. Sales and service applications represent its two largest segments, posting $9.0 billion and $9.8 billion of revenue in fiscal 2026. Together they made up roughly 45% of the company's revenue that year, and each grew by about 8%.

Management has outlined broader ambitions for the business. In September, executives set a target of more than $63 billion in revenue for fiscal 2030. That compares with the $41.5 billion reported for fiscal 2026.

The share price appears to assume some of this growth already. The stock has risen 40% in the past three months, compared with 3.8% for the index. Still, the shares remain 11.5% below their 52-week high.

What Has Salesforce Not Yet Shown Investors?

Salesforce has not yet disclosed how much of Agentforce's revenue comes from customers who are past the trial stage. When asked about this during the August 26 call, management provided a count instead: the company added 2,000 paying customers into production, and said the number of accounts with agents in production grew 70% from the quarter before.

Users can now access Salesforce through tools like Slack without opening the company's dedicated software screens. Management said it is still determining how to charge for that access.

The next earnings report covers fiscal Q3 2027. Salesforce issued revenue guidance of $11.42 billion to $11.5 billion for the quarter, following reported revenue of $11.35 billion in fiscal Q2. The key metrics to watch in that report are the share of sales and service users on premium editions and Agentforce's recurring revenue.

title: What Is Adobe No Longer Telling You?
detail:

Image from Pexels

Adobe (ADBE) stock is priced at 12.9 times earnings, compared to a 21.9 multiple for the S&P 500. Yet even at that valuation, investors need to understand exactly what they hold as corporate priorities shift. Just a year ago, executives highlighted how much of the company's subscription revenue was influenced by AI. They no longer emphasize that measure. So what does Adobe point to now?

Adobe Now Points To A Narrower AI Number

The software maker now spotlights revenue specifically from products sold as AI products, which it brands as AI-first. On the fiscal Q4 2025 call, executives said that total new AI-influenced recurring revenue exceeded one-third of the business, after widening the measure to include the newer AI-first products.

This metric offers a much tighter lens than the previous standard. During the fiscal Q3 2025 call, leadership stated that recurring revenue influenced by AI had passed $5 billion. By the following quarter, executives said their strategy was to drive all recurring revenue through AI-influenced products. That broader measure served to signal that AI was already a component of what many customers were paying for.

Adobe's AI Products Are Still A Small Business

This AI-first recurring revenue accounted for more than 2% of Adobe's $27.5 billion in total recurring revenue during fiscal Q3 2026. The former metric painted a vastly larger picture. On the fiscal Q4 2025 call, executives noted the AI-influenced figure exceeded one-third of all recurring revenue, adding that the newer AI-first products were factored into that total.

Even so, these dedicated AI products are expanding at a much sharper clip than the broader business. Executives reported that AI-first recurring revenue grew more than 150% from a year earlier, while total recurring revenue increased 11.2%. For context, during the fiscal Q1 2025 call, leadership said the AI-first lineup had contributed more than $125 million of recurring revenue.

Customer engagement with the tools is also rising. According to executives, AI usage picked up from the prior quarter across both Creative Cloud and the Firefly app.

Should Adobe Shareholders Welcome The Narrower Number?

Yes, with two caveats. The narrower metric counts only AI products that customers actually pay for, and it is growing quickly, so it is the stricter of the two measures. That provides a reassuring signal for those holding the stock.

The risk lies in the scale of those products. They remain a small fraction of the overall business, meaning the bulk of an investment in Adobe is tied to the rest of the subscription base. At the same time, the company is giving more away to acquire users. Monthly users of its free creative products passed 100 million, up more than 70% from a year earlier. Contracted future revenue grew 8% over the same period. When asked in September about posting the first single-digit growth in that metric since early fiscal 2023, executives tied the pace to their focus on signing up free users, noting the figure steps up in the fourth quarter.

Wall Street is not entirely comfortable with the current growth profile. On October 12, Wells Fargo downgraded the stock, citing worsening organic growth, executive instability, and a loss in pricing power.

While the specialized AI products are expanding rapidly, the wider subscription base remains an unsettled variable. When Adobe reports fiscal Q4, the key number to watch is whether total recurring revenue reaches about $28.3 billion. That is management's target of 10.2% growth on the $25.66 billion it started fiscal 2026 with, against $27.5 billion at the end of the third quarter.
